class_evidence: Stated for two-class problems (Abstract; Sec. 1, p.97); Algorithms 1-2 use labels y in {-1,+1} (pp.98, 100). Two-class 2-D Gaussian simulation (Sec. 5, p.100). 86 binary datasets: 20 HDDT (Table 2, p.102) and 66 KEEL (Table 3, p.103), 5x2-fold CV, J48 (Sec. 6, p.101). Multiclass extension listed as future work only (Sec. 7, p.110).
reduced_multiclass: 66 KEEL sets derived from 16 sources (footnote 7, p.101) as one-vs-rest or merged-group splits (e.g. ecoli-0-1-4-7_vs_2-3-5-6, yeast-2_vs_4, page-blocks-1-3_vs_4); HDDT sets such as letter, pendigits, satimage are presumably binarised, reduction not described.
smote_explanation: Each ensemble member gets a training set of the original size with a random class split (Alg. 1 lines 6-7, p.98): the class that must grow is filled with SMOTE (k = 5; Sec. 3, p.97) and the other is randomly undersampled, and when the split is inverted SMOTE grows the original majority class (Alg. 1 lines 12-15; Sec. 4.1, p.98). Partner and placement are as in SMOTE. Generation is redone for every member of a plain or bagging ensemble, or in every AdaBoost.M2 round (RB-Boost, Alg. 2, Sec. 4.2, p.100).
corrections: Add Seed selection: the oversampled class is random and can be the original majority (Alg. 1 line 15). The proposal also includes stand-alone Random Balance ensembles (E-RB, BAG-RB), not only RB-Boost.
flags: Whether growing the majority class counts as a seed-selection change is debatable.

class_evidence: 8 multiclass datasets with all classes kept: 7 KEEL (Thyroid 3 classes, Lymphography 4, Pageblocks 5, Dermatology 6, Autos 6, Ecoli 8, Yeast 10) and UCI Wine Quality (7) (Sec. 3.1, Table 1). No two-class experiment. 10-fold CV with J48, SMO, Naive Bayes, IBk (Sec. 3).
multiclass_how: Mean class size m is the common target: classes below m are SMOTEd up to m with a per-class rate, classes above m are reduced to m by EM clustering and near-uniform sampling across clusters (Sec. 2, Fig. 1; Sec. 3.1). No decomposition, no ensemble.
smote_explanation: Synthetic points come from standard SMOTE run inside each under-represented class (Fig. 1); the only change is how many points each class gets, enough to reach the mean class size m with a rate computed per class (Sec. 2). Seeds, partners within the class and placement are as in SMOTE, and generation is a one-off step before training. The EM cluster-based undersampling acts on real points of the large classes, not on synthetic ones.
flags: SMOTE k not stated; whether SCUT is applied only to training folds is not stated.
